newsitem.title: USA: Energy Dept reviews lawsuit by states, utilities.
newsitem.headline: Energy Dept reviews lawsuit by states, utilities.

text.p: The U.S. Energy Department said Friday it was reviewing pleadings filed by more than 30 utilities and 46 state agencies seeking court approval for utilities to stop payments into a federal nuclear waste fund and freeze $600 million they have already paid.
Energy Department officials are expected to address the issue at a Senate Energy Committee hearing scheduled for next Wednesday, an Energy Department spokeswoman said.

The lawsuits filed at the U.S. Court of Appeals Friday stemmed from a December announcement by the Energy Department that it would not be able to accept spent fuel from nuclear reactors by January 1998, as required under a 1982 law and reinforced by an appeals court decision last July.
The nuclear waste fund was set up in 1983 for the government to build a permanent dump by January 1998 for high level radioactive waste from commercial reactors,
Utilities want to stop paying an annual $600 million into the fund until the government abides by its end of the law.
